title: Refund that did not come

statutes.title: Who is a consumer
statutes.quote: buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment ... but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose; or hires or avails of any service for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised ... but does not include a person who avails of such service for any commercial purpose. ... the expression commercial purpose does not include use by a person of goods bought and used by him exclusively for the purpose of earning his livelihood, by means of self-employment; ... buys any goods and hires or avails any services includes offline or online transactions through electronic means.
statutes.source: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, section 2(7). Ellipses mark cuts inside a long definition. The words between them are the Act's.

statutes.title: Deficiency
statutes.quote: Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service and includes any act of negligence or omission or commission by such person which causes loss or injury to the consumer; and deliberate withholding of relevant information by such person to the consumer.

statutes.act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
statutes.title: Which commission, based on what you paid
statutes.quote: The District Commission shall have jurisdiction where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees. The State Commission shall have jurisdiction where that value exceeds fifty lakh rupees but does not exceed two crore rupees. The National Commission shall have jurisdiction where that value exceeds two crore rupees.
statutes.source: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, rules 3 to 5, made under the provisos to sections 34, 47 and 58. Confirmed in the PIB release of 30 December 2021. The test is consideration paid, not the compensation you later claim.

statutes.title: Grievance officer timeline
statutes.quote: Every e-commerce entity shall ensure that the grievance officer acknowledges the receipt of any consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redresses the complaint within one month from the date of receipt of the complaint.

statutes.title: Accepted refunds
statutes.quote: Every e-commerce entity shall effect all payments towards accepted refund requests of the consumers as prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India or any other competent authority under any law for the time being in force, within a reasonable period of time, or as prescribed under applicable laws.
statutes.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, rule 4(10). This is not a promise that every cancellation is refundable, and it is not a one-month bank-credit deadline. The one-month period is in rule 4(5), for redress of a complaint.

statutes.title: When a marketplace seller cannot refuse a refund
statutes.quote: No seller offering goods or services through a marketplace e-commerce entity shall refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services purchased or agreed to be purchased, or refuse to refund consideration, if paid, if such goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or if the goods or services are not of the characteristics or features as advertised or as agreed to, or if such goods or services are delivered late from the stated delivery schedule: Provided that in the case of late delivery, this sub-rule shall not be applied if such late delivery was due to force majeure.

explanation: This is a refund of money you already paid, for a good or a service that was not delivered as agreed. What you paid is Rs 2,499. Under the 2021 jurisdiction rules I have loaded, that sits with the District Commission. The test is the consideration you paid, not a compensation number you add later. Because this was an online order, I am also using the E-Commerce Rules, 2020: a marketplace seller is not supposed to refuse a refund for goods that are defective or not as advertised, and the grievance officer has to acknowledge a complaint in forty-eight hours and redress it in one month. That one month is for the complaint, not a promise that the bank credit arrives in one month. A refund they have not even accepted is a different sentence in the same rules, and it says a reasonable period, not a fixed number of days. Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is the definition of deficiency I have loaded: a fault in the performance of a service, including withholding information. The fact you can take forward is that the money was not returned. Whether a commission will agree is not something I can promise.
options: Write to the other side and keep the complaint number. Ask for Rs 2,499 back.
For a packaged good, you can also register it on the National Consumer Helpline, 1915, or consumerhelpline.gov.in, before you file a case.
If that fails, the forum I can point at is the District Commission. Filing is on the e-Jagriti portal. I have not loaded the filing section, so the notice does not cite it.
lawyer: See a lawyer if the other side is a hospital, the amount is large, or you are close to a deadline. I have not loaded the Limitation Act.
opponent: The return window in the policy had closed.
The product was used, so this is not a defect.
We offered a replacement, not money. Read your own invoice before you answer that.

2. Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 treats a fault in the performance of a service, and the withholding of relevant information, as a deficiency.
3. Rule 6(3) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 says a marketplace seller shall not refuse to refund consideration paid where the goods or services are defective, deficient, or not of the characteristics advertised or agreed. Rule 4(5) gives the grievance officer forty-eight hours to acknowledge a complaint and one month to redress it.
4. Refund Rs 2,499 within 15 days. If you do not, I will take advice on a complaint before the District Commission. I am not adding a compensation figure, because the forum depends on what I paid.
